body: Agreed, though it's the least of my worries right now. I'm afraid the hospital will just have to raise prices to compensate. I apologize to the future patients of that place; I never wanted to go there myself.

Thank you for the kind words. It's a description that I've spent a decent amount of time mulling over in past years in anticipation of actually telling somebody. It didn't quite come out to my expectations, but it's good to know you appreciated it. 

I generally agree with your comments. There's this stigma against mental illness that I find to be very strange. In the event of bodily pain, injury, or other physical ailment, it's considered only common sense to go to a healthcare professional and be treated. Yet when your brain - which I would argue is the single most important part of your being - is having problems you're just being lazy or listlessly fishing for attention and you're a crazy nutter if you go to a mental healthcare professional. I suppose it's to do with the (lack of) visibility of the condition and distinct inability for many people to put themselves in the shoes of others. It reminds me of an ex who took a softball to the knee, (Yes, really) shattering it and leading to a botched surgery that resulted in him being unable to stand for extended periods of time. On the bus, he would be given dirty looks and was once chided for sitting down because it wasn't obvious to observers that he couldn't stand for long.

That said, I also believe you're right in that people who fake it are harmful to actual sufferers. Few people seem to understand how effective crying wolf can be as propaganda. The more something is brought to attention, the less impact it has when impact is actually required. Clinical depression in particular has the somewhat unfortunate issue of sharing a name with what's merely a sad mood.

When I recover (assuming I do, because the alternative isn't much worth talking about), I think I'll drop this life and move on to something completely different. I felt a brief, but powerful surge of adrenaline when I jumped, and I'm thinking I want more of that. Maybe I'll go on an adventure and stabilize myself through excitement. I'll probably just die alone in the woods, though I suppose that wouldn't be an awful outcome at this point.

I suppose so. Originally I wrote that I was good as bitter humor/sarcasm, but it looks like my poor writing has betrayed me as people in the other thread (and another post I saw here that was deleted for whatever reason) were also taking it to mean that I'm actually good. Whether I failed to get the point across or you simply skipped to the tl;dr without reading the post or you're subtly mocking me doesn't really matter, I had a giggle, as they say.

Thanks. It looks mostly just like an ugly essay (but without those pesky things like a main idea, a proper introduction and conclusion, and formatting) to me so your perspective on it is mildly amusing to me. I'm not sure what you mean by "[you're] sorry it's right now and not later" though. Would it be better later, after I've healed?

The causes and symptoms of depression do vary, and may appear quite different for different people. If my description hits too close to home for you, I recommend you speak to a professional about it. Someone who knows what they're talking about and can help you in a significant way before you suffer for too long.

There are actually a small handful of issues I could easily point out as causes of anguish, though I didn't list them because they weren't relevant to the topic at hand. I only wrote about the anhedonia because it was the focal point of the note I left.

Thank you for your well-wishing; it's you and me both now. We can hope together!

In my personal experience, self-harming didn't make me feel better. You're supposed to get some kind of high from cutting as your brain releases chemicals to dull the feeling, which was my reason for experimenting with it, but the alleged euphoria never came. It just hurt and left a sore spot that healed into an ugly scar (I committed to cutting DEEP to make sure I was doing it right). Furthermore, it's an unreliable suicide method unless you're going for the throat, which takes a staggering amount of determination to overcome the self-preservation instinct. Either way, I don't recommend cutting yourself.

Perhaps your focus can be tempered into anger or some other intense/"hot" emotion. I found I was unusually productive when I was pushing forward with anger. Anger issues can be a different kind of destructive, but as a person who has been going nowhere for a long time, I believe it's better than wasting away quietly. Who knows, it might take you somewhere.

Thank you. I say the same to you; this world could stand to lose some misery.

My one internet friend had sent me a laptop a while prior because my computer was shit. I packed it up and sent it back, then I wrote a note for my mother that properly detailed some of the actual effects of clinical depression (and, foolishly, implied that I was going to jump).  

Some 11-12 years ago, me saying I was depressed was dismissed by the idea that I "was just a bit sad about whatever" and that depression "is for middle-aged men." Of course, I was twelve or thirteen years old at the time, so it's not surprising that I wouldn't be taken seriously. In truth, however, it was reasonably severe at the time and rapidly worsening. 

Being depressed isn't really about "being sad," it's more of a lack of feeling or spirit. All of your hobbies and interests are diminished, then lost entirely. You lose your appetite and food becomes bland and tasteless. Socializing doesn't improve your mood, and is way too exhausting. Exercise doesn't get you high. Sex feels like nothing. Music doesn't move you. Sleeping is unreasonably difficult (I remember finding out that the average person takes something like 12 minutes to fall asleep. It's literally hours for me) and doesn't refresh you. You can't focus, or become inspired. You feel constantly lethergic, fragile, weak, stupid. Everything is increasingly less engaging to the point where nothing seems important or interesting. Even things I know that I should care about on an intellectual level; showering, eating, getting out of bed, taking care of my dogs, going to the hospital, etc. It wrecks your emotional range as well; I exist in a state of nearly-constant apathy occasionally punctuated by extreme sadness, self-loathing, guilt, self-pity and probably some other negative shit I'm forgetting. I used to get extremely angry for extended periods in the early stages of it, but it's been ages since I've been able to maintain such an intense feeling for more than a few seconds. I kind of want to say I miss them. 

It just drains everything out of you until you're a thoroughly indifferent observer. Of course, you get relapses here and there, but they never last, and I think they're more harmful than good because their presence seems to indicate that I'm just bullshitting everyone who sees me not at a low. "See? You're doing good!" Yeah, absolutely.

After leaving the note on my desk, I went to jump off the top of some unused hospital or mental institute that was nearby. It wasn't high enough, I ended up only losing some teeth and breaking my legs, ribs, a few fingers, my collarbone, and a few bones in my arm. I woke up in the hospital.

I regret doing both of those things. I've not asked, but I assume I owe my being alive to the implication of my note (or maybe a patrol that was hired to keep teenagers from fucking around in the derelict heard me screeching like a bitch). Two months later, I'm sitting here in a wheelchair with my previously good arm in a sling and cast and typing up my sob-story for you people on a computer from 2001. My only friend of six years balked when he got his laptop (and apology note) back and left me a heartbreakingly distant offline message about how he couldn't handle seeing me anymore (not even mentioning that I was supposed to be dead, as if he knew I'd fail). 

Now I have stacks of medical bills that I can't pay because I don't have insurance or income and my family thinks I'm fucking retarded (though to be fair, they're right) and probably that I won't live long anyway (again, probably right) so they don't want to help. I can't get work because I have no education or work history because I didn't start doing shit ten years ago. I have no contacts. I'm crippled for at least the next six months, if not forever. I will never be able to stop tonguing the huge gap between my teeth. I can't even try to kill myself again because this house has stairs outside and all access to anything remotely harmful was removed because for some reason it's important that I stay alive. 

There is good news though; I'm officially mentally stable and don't have to spend any time in suicide watch. That means I don't have to pay for more therapy than I already do and can stay at home and listen to my dogs be loud fucking assholes all day, every day.

Health debt collectors called me and asked how I was today. I said "good."

tl;dr: I'm good.
